correctness.rationale: Cell stabilizers fix every word position, so the orbit CW incidence counts are signed deletion counts with no stabilizer factors. The unused-letter transposition fixes a short word, not a full extension as one sentence suggests; it adjusts parity and proves transitivity up to length n−2. In the last two lengths parity gives two cells. Moving the deleted letter to the end changes parity by (−1)^(n−i); combining this with the face sign gives the displayed odd matrix and the even matrix with image generated by (n/2)(e−o). Inductively, the one-cell skeleton alternates between contractible even stages and odd spheres: a unit boundary is a degree-one map to the previous sphere. For n≥4 the resulting middle skeleton is a sphere (even n) or a wedge of two spheres (odd n). Here Hurewicz identifies the actual top attaching maps with their degrees; invertible basis changes on source and target wedges preserve homotopy cofibers. Odd Smith factors are 1,n, while even degrees are opposite signs of n/2. For n=3, attach the first relator ab⁻¹a first and eliminate the edge b, which occurs exactly once in this cell before the other attachment. The other relator then becomes a degree-three loop on the surviving circle. Thus the proof establishes the homotopy types, not just the homology matrices. The supplied orbit/Smith script was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the universal result.
residual_risks: Only the full ordinary orbit space is classified; the argument is not a Borel or subgroup classification.
